stem:
An experiment is conducted to determine the effect of tonicity of the solutions on red blood cells. Image II represents the condition of RBCs after keeping them in different concentration of solutions in beaker I, II and III for a particular time.

The option that CORRECTLY identifies the tonicity of the solutions in beaker I, II and III is

| Option | Beaker I | Beaker II | Beaker III |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| A | hypertonic | hypotonic | isotonic |
| B | isotonic | hypotonic | hypertonic |
| C | hypotonic | hypertonic | isotonic |
| D | isotonic | hypertonic | hypotonic |

options.A: Beaker I: hypertonic; Beaker II: hypotonic; Beaker III: isotonic
options.B: Beaker I: isotonic; Beaker II: hypotonic; Beaker III: hypertonic
options.C: Beaker I: hypotonic; Beaker II: hypertonic; Beaker III: isotonic
options.D: Beaker I: isotonic; Beaker II: hypertonic; Beaker III: hypotonic

explanation: In Beaker I, red blood cells retain their normal biconcave disc morphology, demonstrating an isotonic medium (net zero water movement). In Beaker II, RBCs swell and haemolyse/burst due to endosmosis, confirming a hypotonic medium. In Beaker III, RBCs lose water by exosmosis and become shrivelled/crenated, confirming a hypertonic medium. Thus, Option B is correct.

stem:
Consider the given cubes as cells.

Which of the following graphs CORRECTLY represents the relationship between the side length of cells and their surface area to volume ratio?
(Note: Graphs are not to scale.)

options.A: Curve A showing non-linear decrease of SA:V ratio as side length increases from 1 cm to 3 cm.
options.B: Graph B showing linear increase of SA:V ratio as side length increases.
options.C: Graph C showing constant SA:V ratio as side length changes.
options.D: Graph D showing parabolic increase of SA:V ratio as side length increases.

explanation: For a cube of side length s, surface area is 6s^2 and volume is s^3, giving a surface area to volume ratio of 6/s. This is accurately depicted by Curve A.

stem:
In a laboratory, a group of students was investigating the action of amylase on starch solution keeping the pH neutral. They used iodine as a chemical indicator. One of the group members added a chemical that drastically decreased the pH of solution in the test tube.

Which of the following conditions will occur due to this drastic change in pH?

options.C: Starch and amylase will bind strongly.
options.D: Iodine colour will change into dark blue.

answer_review_note: Official key accepts both A and D
explanation: Salivary and pancreatic amylase function optimally near neutral pH (pH 6.8–7.0). Drastically lowering the pH disrupts the hydrogen and ionic bonds stabilizing the enzyme's tertiary active site structure, causing irreversible denaturation (Option A). Because the denatured amylase can no longer hydrolyse starch, unhydrolysed starch remains present in the tube, causing iodine indicator to remain/change to dark blue-black (Option D). The official examination board key accepts both A and D.

stem: In human stomach, the factor that makes salivary amylase dysfunctional is the

options.B: secretion of pepsinogen from the stomach wall.
options.C: churning and mixing action of stomach muscles.
options.D: formation of protection barrier by mucus in the stomach wall.

explanation: Salivary amylase operates optimally at near-neutral pH (6.8). In the stomach, gastric glands secrete hydrochloric acid (HCl), lowering gastric juice pH to 1.5–2.0. This intense acidity denatures the protein conformation of salivary amylase, terminating its enzymatic activity. Pepsinogen is an inactive zymogen, churning is mechanical, and mucus protects the epithelium.

options.B: the synthesis of food in mesophyll cells.
options.C: transportation of water from roots to leaves.
options.D: translocation of glucose from leaves to roots.

explanation: Evaporation of water from leaf mesophyll surfaces through stomata into the air generates negative hydrostatic pressure (suction tension) in leaf xylem. stem: In contrast to the blood pressure in aorta, the blood pressure in the pulmonary arteries is lower because

options.A: pulmonary arteries carry blood away from the heart.
options.B: the distance between the lungs and the heart is short.
options.C: the size of lumen of the pulmonary arteries is narrow.

explanation: The pulmonary circuit is a low-resistance, low-pressure vascular bed because the lungs are located directly adjacent to the heart within the thoracic cavity (very short anatomical distance).
